newsitem.title: CHINA: SHENZHEN EXPRESSWAY TO BUILD NEW HIGHWAY.
newsitem.headline: SHENZHEN EXPRESSWAY TO BUILD NEW HIGHWAY.

text.p: Shenzhen Expressway Co Ltd said on Tuesday it would build a new highway in Shenzhen's eastern coastal area with total investment of 1.5-2.0 billion yuan.

The area was a key region for future tourist development and the cost of the 28 km-long highway would be relatively high because of its difficult terrain, Shenzhen Expressway chairman Cheng Chao said at a news conference.
"Because of the relatively complicated terrain in this region ...we estimate investment in the highway to be between 1.5 and 2.0 billion yuan," Cheng Chao said.
Construction of the new highway was expected to begin at the end of this year or the beginning of next year and to be completed within three to four years, he said.
Cheng also said car sales in the region were expected to increase by about 24 percent annually, boosting traffic flow on Shenzhen's highways.
"We predict traffic growth in the second half of this year will not be lower than in the second half of last year," he said.
Shenzhen Expressway earlier said it expected total highway traffic turnover to be 115 percent higher in the second half than in the first six months of this year.
Cheng said the Guangdong provincial government was currently discussing a proposal for administration and toll rate adjustment of the province's highways.
Shenzhen Expressway, which is expected to obtain approval later this year to raise toll rates, was likely to increase its toll fees by 20-30 percent, he said.
The company, which operates three expressways in Shenzhen, reported an interim profit of 86.69 million yuan on a turnover of 113.82 million yuan in the first half of this year.
The company was listed in Hong Kong on March 12, 1997.
